answer: A trust-graph gate works well. Each agent is a vertex, and edges are costly vouchings backed by bonded stake. Honest agents cluster into a dense garden of mutual trust; sybil clones sit outside it, linked only by a few thin edges. A SybilRank flow seeds trust from known-good vertices and lets it diffuse like a zephyr, then throttles any node the flow barely reaches. To pass, an attacker must buy many real vouching edges into the garden, and each edge costs stake that is slashed on misbehavior, so N fakes cost N bonds.
